newsitem.title: UK: UK reviewing contracting out of prison management.
newsitem.headline: UK reviewing contracting out of prison management.

text.p: The new Labour government is considering what to do about contracting-out prison management, but existing contracts will be honoured, Home Secretary Jack Straw said on Thursday in a written parliamentary answer.
Straw said the government had expressed concern about the principle of contracting-out of prison management and was considering ways to strengthen the current regulatory framework.

But he said the government would give "careful consideration" to a parliamentary Home Affairs Select Committee report earlier this year which said the idea was proving a success and should be developed further.
Straw said the government's immediate approach to new contracts and the renewal of existing contracts was determined by current expenditure plans and operational needs.
But before long-term plans could be made, Straw said the prison service had to examine ways of using private finance to give value for money.
If the prison service wanted to take back management of contracted-out prisons, it had to show it had the capacity to match the performance of the private sector, he added.
The Wolds Prison in Humberside, north-east England, became the first to be privately run in Britain in 1992 when Group 4, a part of the private Dutch firm Group 4 Securitas, took charge.

Other companies currently involved in the field are UK Detention Services, whose main shareholder is Corrections Corp of America, and Premier Prisons, a joint venture between Wackenhut Corrections Corp and Serco Group Plc.
Securicor Group Plc leads a joint venture which will run one of three private prisons currently being built.
To return prisons to public management, the prison service would have to show a case based on value for money, he said.

Private sector involvement in other areas of the prison service which did not affect the principle that jailed offenders should be the responsibility of the state would be treated on their merits, he said.

Straw said that as a result of this, the government had authorised the extension of a contract with Group 4 for court escort and custody services in northern England. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
